title: Reviewing the New Analyst
briefing: Priya has hired a graduate, Sam Delacroix, and asked you to review Sam's first assessment before it goes to the Risk Committee: a cyber risk entry for the route-planning system.
The assessment has real problems. How you review it matters as much as what you find.

context.text: Hollis has approved a quote request for the spoilage insurance layer you proposed. Your reputation for clear quantitative work is growing.

evidence.title: Sam's draft register entry (R-031)
body: Title: Cyber attack. Cause: hackers. Event: cyber attack. Consequence: bad things happen.
Inherent L5 x I5. Controls: firewall (effective), antivirus (effective). Residual L1 x I2 (Low). Owner: IT.

evidence.title: IT facts Sam had access to
evidence.body: Route planning runs on a vendor cloud service. No offline fallback: without it, dispatch takes about 4x longer by hand. Multi-factor login is enabled for admins only. The last restore test was 18 months ago.

evidence.title: Note from Sam
evidence.body: I wasn't sure how to rate it so I used what felt right. Happy for any feedback!

questions.prompt: Which problems in Sam's entry must be fixed before it goes to committee?

options.label: Cause, event and consequence are too vague to manage ("hackers", "bad things")
Residual falls from 25 to 2 with no evidence the controls work
The controls listed don't address the real exposure: no offline fallback, admin-only MFA, untested restore
Owner 'IT' is a department, not an accountable person
The entry is too long
options.feedback: It is too vague, not too long.

questions.prompt: Which event statement is the best rewrite?

options.label: "Route planning unavailable for over 24 hours (vendor ransomware or account takeover), forcing manual dispatch"
options.feedback: Specific, measurable, and links causes to an operational consequence.

options.label: "Cyber attack on Valtren's IT estate causing disruption to operations and customer service"
options.feedback: Still generic: what fails and for how long?

options.label: "Criminal hackers target Valtren's systems through phishing emails, weak passwords or unpatched software"
options.feedback: That is a cause, not an event.

questions.prompt: How do you give Sam the feedback?

options.label: Sit together: ask Sam to explain the rating, point to the IT facts, rewrite one part together, let Sam redo the rest
options.feedback: Sam learns the method, keeps ownership, and you check understanding.

options.label: Rewrite it yourself for committee, then walk Sam through the changes afterwards
options.feedback: Fast, but Sam learns nothing and will make the same mistakes next time.

options.label: Return the draft with detailed tracked changes and a comment explaining the reason for each correction
options.feedback: Accurate but impersonal; a first-time analyst needs the reasoning, not just corrections.

options.label: Let it go to committee: challenge from senior people will teach Sam more than you can
options.feedback: Exposes a junior colleague and puts a misleading entry in front of the committee.

questions.prompt: Committee papers are due tomorrow and the redo won't be ready. What do you do?

options.label: Pull R-031 from this month's pack, tell Priya why, and bring a proper entry next month
options.feedback: Better one month late than wrong in front of the committee.

options.label: Submit Sam's draft marked 'provisional' and bring the corrected version next month
options.feedback: A Low rating on an untested restore and no fallback could mislead the committee.

options.label: Rewrite it overnight yourself so the committee sees a proper entry on time
options.feedback: Meets the deadline, but takes the learning away from Sam.

questions.prompt: Who should own the rewritten risk?

options.label: The Head of Logistics Systems, who owns the vendor contract and the dispatch process
options.feedback: The person who can fund and decide the fallback.

options.label: The IT Manager, Mei Lin, since every control involved is an IT control she runs
The risk team, until the business accepts ownership of a cyber risk
options.feedback: Risk owners manage the risk; analysts assess it.

lesson: Review to teach, not just to correct. Specific events, evidenced controls and a named owner make a risk entry useful; vague entries give false comfort.
